test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Motor Vehicle) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When the crank is at the dead centre, what will be the magnitude of bending moment and twisting moment at the crankshaft?

options.text: Both bending moment and twisting moment on the shaft are maximum
Bending moment on the shaft is maximum and the twisting moment is zero.
Bending moment on the shaft is minimum and the twisting moment is maximum.
Both bending moment and the twisting moment are zero in the shaft

solution:
The correct answer is __Bending moment on the shaft is maximum and the twisting moment is zero.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the dead centre position of the crankshaft__, the twisting moment becomes zero as there is no angular displacement of the crank.
 
• The bending moment reaches its maximum value at this position due to the forces acting on the crankshaft.
 
• This condition is significant in analyzing the design and strength of the crankshaft.
 
• Engineers ensure that the crankshaft can withstand maximum bending moments to prevent failure or deformation.
 
• The dead centre position refers to the extreme end of the piston's movement in the cylinder.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Bending Moment:**

 
 
• The bending moment is a measure of the internal forces caused by bending stresses within a beam or shaft.
 
• It is critical in mechanical engineering to ensure structural integrity.
 
 
 
• **Twisting Moment:**
 
 
• The twisting moment refers to the torque applied to a shaft due to rotational forces.
 
• It is important to consider while designing rotating components such as crankshafts.
